the QacR protein is induced by a coil-to-helices transition that causes a conformational change in a multidrug binding pocket that is formed by multiple aromatic and polar amino acid residues and glutamate residues.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
QacR is a novel multidrug-binding transcription factor that uses a novel mechanism of multidrug recognition and induction, which is distinct from the mechanism of multidrug transport.
the QacR-drugs complexes provide a structural basis for the molecular mechanisms of drug recognition and the induction of the multidrug binding protein, QacR.
QacR represents a new class of multidrug-binding proteins that are structurally distinct from multidrug transporters, but that the two classes of proteins have similar multidrug-binding mechanisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have determined the structure of QacR bound to six different drugs and that these structures show how the protein is induced to a high affinity state and that this is achieved by the formation of a large binding pocket that is capable of binding multiple drugs.

the structural basis of QacR induction by structurally diverse drugs involves a single protein that binds drugs at two distinct sites and that the drug-binding pocket is formed through a coil-to-helical transition that is induced by the binding of the drugs.
QacR is a member of a family of transcriptional repressors, which includes the TetR family, the MarR family, and the LysR family.
The main takeaway from our work is that
QacR is an inducible multidrug repressor that binds drugs with a multisite mechanism, which is likely to be common to other multidrug resistance regulators.
the QacR protein has the ability to bind multiple drugs, which is consistent with the broad substrate range of the QacA efflux transporter.
QacR, and perhaps other transcription factors, can recognize multiple drugs simultaneously.
